results.title: Concurso de Cante Jondo
results.text: El Concurso del Cante Jondo (Contest of the Deep Song) was a well-known celebration of the art of flamenco, its music, song, and dance, held in Granada, on Corpus Christi, the 13th and 14 June 1922. At conception the idea of composer Manuel de Falla, its organizating activities enjoyed early and strong support from poet Federico García Lorca. The two outdoor, evening events included amateur flamenco performers, as well as revered professionals.

results.title: Ignacio Mondaca Romero
results.text: Ignacio Mondaca Romero (born 1956) is a Mexican writer who has written a large number of articles, essays, literary criticism and books. He was born in San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora, Mexico. His work has won the Concurso Nacional de Cuento in 1998, the Concurso del Libro Sonorense in 2003 and in 2009. Major works include "El pianoforte", "Relatos de ocio", "El diluvio y otros cuentos", "Cuentos para llevar", "Brevedad vital", "Ensayos del desaire" and "Crónicas de una ciudad despierta". Mondaca was the president of the Escritores de Sonora, A.C. writers organization from 2006 to 2010.

results.title: Cante jondo
results.text: Cante jondo ( ] ) is a vocal style in flamenco, an unspoiled form of Andalusian folk music. The name means "deep song" in Spanish, with "hondo" ("deep") spelled with J (] ) as a form of eye dialect, because traditional Andalusian pronunciation has retained an aspirated H lost in other forms of Spanish.
